# `Q-2-10` — Closing Quote Without Matching Open Quote

> A closing single-quote mark appears with no opening
> single-quote earlier in the block.

## What this means

Quarto markdown treats single quotes as a paired construct: a
`'` preceded by a word-character is read as a closing quote.
When the parser sees a closing position without an earlier
matching open, it raises this error.

The diagnostic message points at the closing quote as the
trigger; the actual mistake is usually the missing opening
quote.

## Why this happens

The most common cause is a contraction or possessive — `it's`,
`don't`, `Mary's` — where the apostrophe is being read as a
closing quote. The parser distinguishes apostrophes from quote
marks by surrounding context, and a stray space can flip the
interpretation.

## How to fix

If the mark is an apostrophe, ensure no spurious whitespace
precedes it. If the construction really is a quotation, add the
opening `'` at the intended start.

For literal apostrophes that the parser keeps mis-reading,
escape them:

```markdown
The variable \'x\' (treated literally).
```

## Example

```markdown
a' b.
```

The `'` after `a` is read as a closing quote with no opener.
